A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KL-estimation research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and relocated or renamed material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-2/IMDB estimator comparisons and RLHF experiments, including Table 1, training curves and Pareto-front analysis.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds a gradient-norm variance experiment in Section 5.2 and UltraFeedback results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Both versions use tokenwise Rao–Blackwellized KL estimation, the corresponding gradient estimator and importance-weighted off-policy estimation. The revised exposition, notation and implementation illustration do not establish a new algorithmic component or changed procedure.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates sentiment-controlled generation using GPT-2 and IMDB. v3 retains this coverage and adds UltraFeedback prompts with Zephyr-7B-Beta and Mistral-7B-v0.1 in Appendix E, substantially extending evaluation beyond the movie-review domain.

E2.justification: The estimator comparison still includes MC, Horvitz–Thompson, optimally calibrated CV, CV with alpha = 1, and RB. RLHF still compares MC against RB. The new UltraFeedback table uses the same comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 adds a 40-prompt gradient comparison with matched prompts and model initializations. Its additional UltraFeedback protocol uses 512 prompts, 100 responses per prompt and half-precision inference with 7B models. These are additional protocols; the original DPO setup and RLOO hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds a focused diagnostic measuring MC versus RB gradient-norm variance. The existing prompt-sentiment, sample-size and training-dynamics analyses remain; the three-prompt analysis moves from v1 Figure 1 to v3 Appendix E, Figure 4.

E5.justification: v3 explicitly reports five repetitions for the new gradient-norm variance experiment. The existing estimator repetitions, five-run RLHF uncertainty bands and Pareto permutation tests are retained; there is no reported increase in repetitions for those retained experiments.

E6.justification: v3 adds Table 2's UltraFeedback results and gradient-norm variances of 59.90 for MC versus 45.44 for RB, a reported 24.6% reduction. The new benchmark shows modest RB standard-deviation reductions and ties at M = 10. Table 1 is unchanged. The Pareto percentage changes from 76% to 78% in prose and caption, correcting agreement with the unchanged figure's 0.78 statistic.

T1.justification: v3 adds proofs concerning alpha = 1's unique nonnegativity guarantee and the variance-reducing alpha interval, while removing v1's Bregman-divergence derivation. It also removes finite-cross-entropy assumptions from local-KL and gradient results. Theorem 2 now assumes only finite MC variance, although Appendix C, Eq. (39b), still invokes finite RB variance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: an unbiased RB estimator with variance no greater than MC, an analogous gradient estimator, and more stable RLHF with favorable reward–KL tradeoffs. Additional experiments support these retained claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds explicit limitations explaining why RLHF training experiments remain confined to controlled generation. Appendix E attributes bias in the additional HT/CV results to half precision. Section 3 also explains why correlations between summands require more than a direct application of ordinary Rao–Blackwellization.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds an MC/RB implementation snippet and reports approximately 20 minutes per RLHF experiment on one RTX 4090. Appendix E documents the additional models and precision setting. Existing RLOO hyperparameters and the repository link remain, although v3 no longer explicitly identifies the 512 IMDB examples as coming from the evaluation split.

R1.justification: v3 adds foundational Rao and Blackwell references, Hoogeboom for the undecidability discussion, and UltraFeedback, Mistral and Zephyr citations. References associated with the removed Bregman and language-process discussions disappear. The central positioning relative to existing KL estimators and RLHF libraries remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main exposition is substantially rewritten: application bullets become compact prose, control-variate subsections are consolidated, and Section 3 becomes an estimator-first presentation with a three-step proof sketch. Appendices are reorganized, the prompt analysis moves out of the main text, and limitations and a conference checklist are added.

P2.justification: The main document changes from two columns to a single-column format with substantially different equation, figure and table placement. Existing plot graphics are retained but resized and relocated, including the three-prompt figure's move to Appendix E. v3 also adds Table 2 and a formatted code listing.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful broader-domain evidence, a gradient diagnostic, implementation and compute details, and explicit limitations. It also corrects the Pareto percentage. However, v1's central variance theorem explicitly assumed finite RB variance; v3 removes that assumption while its proof still invokes it in Eq. (39b). The empirical and documentation gains coexist with unresolved support for the broadened theoretical guarantee, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
